**14** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via setup.access (literal, a string literal in readPermission))_

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/mcp/src/connect-ui.ts`, `packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **11** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **61** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 959c26be1f4179202b0ed42f58076190d4d590d5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `02f084bf16ccb44db778d972e6ead6eb1bfaa291` — the merge of head `74c2ef82638a525260943246260fcd7f2fd6902a` into base `959c26be1f4179202b0ed42f58076190d4d590d5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 02f084bf16ccb44db778d972e6ead6eb1bfaa291 && git checkout 02f084bf16ccb44db778d972e6ead6eb1bfaa291
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 959c26be1f4179202b0ed42f58076190d4d590d5 74c2ef82638a525260943246260fcd7f2fd6902a && git checkout -B drift-repro 959c26be1f4179202b0ed42f58076190d4d590d5 && git merge --no-ff 74c2ef82638a525260943246260fcd7f2fd6902a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 959c26be1f4179202b0ed42f58076190d4d590d5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 959c26be1f4179202b0ed42f58076190d4d590d5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Check-runs on this head.** Success: Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Test UI, Build Docs, Check Changeset (first run), Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, PR-body guards (both), Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Auto Label, Check PR Size, filter. Those pending conclusions are gate verdicts this record does not supply.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Removed public export `featureFlagsSettingsManifest` — right.** At the merge base it is reachable from `@objectstack/service-settings`'s one published entry: `package.json` `exports["."]` maps to `dist/index.d.ts` / `dist/index.js`, generated from `src/index.ts`, whose line 164 re-exported the name from `./manifests/index.js` (line 8 there). At head it is absent from both barrels and the declaring file is deleted. Repo-wide `git grep` at base and head finds no importer outside `packages/services/service-settings` itself (three of its own test files, all rewritten in this diff); `ui/`, `examples/`, `apps/`, `packages/qa` import nothing of it. The compiler-carried break lands only on an external host; the changeset names it.
2. **`builtinSettingsManifests` 10 → 9 — right, and a behaviour change on a still-exported aggregate.** The plugin defaults to it (`settings-service-plugin.ts:201`), so every host on the default slate loses the namespace at boot. Named in the changeset's FROM line. The three count pins that read the aggregate (`settings-visibility-declaration` 10→9 with a reason, `settings-retired-workspace-noun` floor 10→9, `settings-translation-coverage` floor 10→9) move with it; the 96-predicate pin is unchanged because the removed manifest declared no `visible`.
3. **The four settable keys `feature_flags.ai_enabled` / `kanban_swimlanes` / `realtime_cursors` / `inline_comments` — removed, accept set to nothing, right.** With no manifest registered, `SettingsService.getManifest`, `get`, `getMany`, `getNamespace`, `set`, `setMany`, `resetNamespace` all refuse through `UnknownNamespaceError` (`code: SETTINGS_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE`, `settings-service.types.ts:561`); the REST door maps that class to `404 UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE` on GET, PUT and action (`settings-routes.ts:312, 373, 433`). The changeset's wire and in-process codes match the tree. Pinned by the new test `no longer serves the retired feature_flags namespace`, which registers every built-in manifest with `OS_FEATURE_FLAGS_AI_ENABLED=true` in the env.
4. **The namespace itself — removed, right.** `GET /api/settings` lists `service.listManifests(ctx)` only (`settings-routes.ts:277`), so the hub no longer offers it. Side effect not named anywhere: `feature_flags` was the only manifest with `category: 'Beta'` / `beta: true`, so the hub's Beta category disappears with it — harmless, consistent with the ruling.
5. **Setup nav entry `nav_settings_feature_flags` with 4 locale labels and 3 source-hash rows — removed, right.** The entry carried no permission gate, so it was served to every Setup reader and pointed at a URL that now 404s; removing it with the page is what the seat amendment (option A) ordered. No remaining reference under `packages/` or `ui/` (source, tests, generated bundles). `settings-branding-posture.pin.test.ts` re-anchors its ordering control on `nav_settings_lifecycle`, the real last platform-objects Configuration entry at head. The `platform-objects.test.ts:515` pin is a floor, not a count.
6. **Locale bundles — `settingsBuiltinTranslations` and the four exported locale objects lose the `feature_flags` block — right.** service-settings carries no generated bundle, so no regeneration was owed there.
7. **`OS_FEATURE_FLAGS_*` environment variables and stored `sys_setting` rows become inert — right, and tolerated by every path that walks stored rows.** `upgrade-impact-report.ts:85-86, 672-681` deliberately does not judge a stored setting whose namespace no manifest registers; `sys-secret-orphan-report.ts:326` classes an unknown `(namespace, key)` as `unattributable` and never throws (the manifest declared no encrypted specifier anyway); `organization-ownership-apply.ts`'s settings-move step selects by `scope = 'global'`, never by manifest (the manifest was `scope: 'tenant'`); `cloud-connection/runtime-config-plugin.ts:1276` reads `branding` alone; `resolve-authz-context.ts:3017` reads `localization` alone. No list-all, export or sync path resolves an arbitrary stored namespace through `getManifest`.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` on `@objectstack/service-settings` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` — right.** Post-Task Checklist step 3: the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone; `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a breaking non-protocol change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. `check-changeset-no-major` forbids `major` in any case. Both bumped packages are the two whose published behaviour moves; the comment-only edits in `mcp`, `plugin-security`, `service-datasource` and the `cli` README line publish no behaviour and need no bump (dev deviation 2, accepted).
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — right.** No spec key, accepted value, metadata type or authorable spelling changes; a settings key is an administrator's saved value, and the nav entry is shipped platform metadata, not an authorable key. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is present and identical on the PR body and the changeset.
- **ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (runtime-export-retired @objectstack/service-settings#featureFlagsSettingsManifest)` — right, judged against D9's three predicates.** Predicate 1 (retired-from-entry): shown in ① item 1. Predicate 2 (no-metadata-surface): at base the operand is declared in `manifests/feature-flags.manifest.ts`, not a `*.zod.ts`, not under `packages/spec/src/contracts/`, not an object definition, not a Zod projection, and no metadata surface references it in code. Predicate 3 (from-operands-named): `readFromBlock` reads one FROM side, the code span `featureFlagsSettingsManifest` between FROM and TO on the body's last line — exactly the marker's operand. The "Removed keys" bullet carries no FROM/TO pair, arrow or mapping table, so it is left to the residual prescription detector; the dev reports that gate green on both local heads, and its CI verdict is the pending second `Check Changeset` run.
- **The dev's deviation on the FROM block (keys moved to a "Removed keys" bullet, FROM line names the export only) — forced and correct.** D9 predicate 3 refuses any FROM operand the marker does not name as out of range, and a settings key is neither operand kind (`package#Export` or `package#Type.member`), so a per-key FROM line was never admissible under this category. The TO side ("drop it from the host's `SettingsServicePlugin({ manifests })` list") is the one-line host fix a removal owes, and the BREAKING banner names both affected parties.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR body: "the cloud repository is not readable from this seat, so a reader there is not ruled out" — escalated to the seat.** A cloud-side read of `feature_flags.*` through the settings client or REST would now get `SETTINGS_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE` / `404 UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE`. Before landing, grep `objectstack-ai/cloud` for `feature_flags`, `FEATURE_FLAGS_` and `featureFlagsSettingsManifest`; the tree here is clean either way.
- **PR body: "Skills-docs: follow-up #30275" for `skills/objectstack-platform/references/plugin-development.md:354-356` — stated by the dev, not verified here** (that issue is outside this review's inputs). The skill text still names the `feature_flags` manifest as the home for org-tunable toggles; `skills/**` is Tier H and was outside the dev's surface. The seat confirms the follow-up exists.
- **Report deviation 1 (changeset FROM block) — answered in ②: right.**
- **Report deviation 2 (no bump for comment-only packages) — answered in ②: accepted.**
- **Report deviation 3 (model-free trailer pair on the thread branch) — a commit-message matter, not a tree matter; noted, nothing to judge here.**
- **Report deviation 4 and `dogfood_battery` (one red in `permission-set-clone-door.dogfood.test.ts`, also red with this diff reverted; attributed to 490d136f2 / #30222; carrier #30108 seat 2) — not this PR's.** The control leg the dev ran is the right shape (same file, 19 source files restored to origin/main, force-rebuilt). Escalated only as: the seat confirms the main-red is on that lane's board before this PR arms the queue (AGENTS.md main-red convention). The head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run is green.
- **`open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.**
- **`out_of_scope_findings` — the four listed are agreed** (the dogfood red; the skills reference; docs.objectos.ai's `FEATURE_FLAGS_AI_ENABLED`; ADR-0007's worked example). On ADR-0007: its decision is the manifest-plus-KV mechanism; Example 3 and Phase 1 item 10 use `feature_flags` as an instance, so removing that instance reverses no recorded decision and no amendment is owed under Prime Directive 13. **Three more that the report does not list — see ④ should-fix 2, 3 and 4** (two stale `packages/spec` comments, the console's Settings-hub subtitle, the `sys_setting.namespace` field description).
- **Acceptance notes on `packages/spec` test fixtures and the console `SettingsField.infoBanner-12671.test.tsx` using `feature_flags` as a self-contained string — agreed:** none imports the removed manifest, and each passes on its own fixture.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the card's ruling ("Remove the four toggles, and the settings page if it is left empty. A flag comes back with the feature that reads it."), ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove, and the code each hunk cites. The premise re-checked on this head: `git grep` for the four keys across `packages/`, `ui/`, `examples/`, `apps/`, `scripts/` (source and tests, generated bundles included) finds no reader — only the new pin, the ADR-0007 example, dated audit prose, and fixture strings in spec/console tests that never touch the manifest. `AppHeader.tsx`'s `aiAssistant` is a label key; the console's `features` map comes from `/api/v1/auth/config`. The ruling's second sentence is honoured: nothing was wired, all four were removed, and the then-empty page (a beta banner and two empty groups) went with them.

- `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/feature-flags.manifest.ts`, `manifests/index.ts`, `src/index.ts` — hold. The removal is total (declaration, aggregate, barrel), leaves no re-export behind an `export *`, and the comment in `src/index.ts` now names the manifests that remain.
- `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts` — holds. The option doc now names `builtinSettingsManifests` instead of a list that was already stale; no behaviour change.
- `packages/services/service-settings/src/translations/*.ts` and `settings-translation-coverage.test.ts` — hold. The `en.ts` header now names the manifests it mirrors; the floor moved with the aggregate.
- `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.test.ts` — holds. The new pin asserts the three faces of the refusal (aggregate, `getManifest`, `get`) with the retired env var set, so a re-registration or an env-only resurrection would red it. The rewritten tests keep their original purpose on `ai.log_prompts` (default false) and `ai.trace_enabled` (default true), which exist on `aiSettingsManifest` at head.
- `settings-branding-posture.pin.test.ts`, `settings-help-business-words.pin.test.ts`, `settings-retired-workspace-noun.pin.test.ts`, `settings-visibility-declaration.pin.test.ts` — hold; each count moves once with its reason written beside it. The business-words header keeps `OS_FEATURE_FLAGS_AI_ENABLED` as a historical example of the shape the sweep refuses, under a new line saying the namespace is gone — history, not a dead pointer.
- `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts` and `translations/*` (labels and source hashes) — hold. No dead link: the entry, its four labels and the three hashes leave together, and nothing under `ui/` or `packages/` names `nav_settings_feature_flags`.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts` — holds. Comment only; the replacement list (`branding`, `company`, `localization`) is exactly the set of built-in manifests declaring `readPermission: 'setup.access'` at head. No permission set, seed or grant names the namespace anywhere in `packages/`.
- `packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/connect-ui.ts` — hold. Comment only; the texts no longer name a Setup page that does not exist.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json` — **does not hold; see must-fix 1.**

**Must-fix**

1. **`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json` is left self-contradictory inside the one item the diff edits.** Item `platform-core.settings-hub-roundtrip` now says at line 788 "the 10 open-framework settings namespaces a stock boot serves: the 9 in builtinSettingsManifests", but line 796 still instructs "capture the visible manifests (the 11 open-framework namespaces above …)" and the scored clause at line 885 still reads "each of the 11 open-framework namespaces resolves GET /api/settings/:ns". A QA run scores that clause against a namespace that no longer exists. The hunk's own claim ("11 namespaces to 10, list and variants") is not what the tree says. Fix: change both `11` to `10` in that item (two numbers; `check-platform-checklist` does not read the prose, so nothing else moves).
